title: Yissachar of Kefar Magdi
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: He is mentioned in [Yerushalmi Rosh Hashanah, chapter 1, halakhah 3](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Rosh_Hashanah.1.3.4), expounding “And He saw iniquity,” etc. [Bereshit Rabbah 52:5](https://www.sefaria.org/Bereshit_Rabbah.52.5) and [74:7](https://www.sefaria.org/Bereshit_Rabbah.74.7) name Rabbi Chama son of Rabbi Chanina and Rabbi Yissachar of Kefar Mandi. If so, he belonged to the second generation of the amoraim of the Land of Israel.[^1][^2]

His expositions are also mentioned in Tanchuma, Vayishlach 24 and Bamidbar 10; Vayikra Rabbah 1:13; Bamidbar Rabbah 20:3; Esther Rabbah, at the end of chapter 7; Shir HaShirim Rabbah, chapter 2, with the printed locator פ״ד; and Midrash Tehillim 5:8 and 10:3.[^3]

notes.text: The native notice on PDF page 7 (printed 840) preserves Magdi in the heading and Mandi in the body; those two forms are not silently reconciled. The checked Guggenheimer Rosh Hashanah passage has Yissachar of Kefar Mendi. The TE Bereshit Rabbah 52:5 has Mandi, while 74:7 has Magdei. These are version spellings, not a new geographic identification.

The accepted Hebrew cites Bereshit Rabbah 52:6 and 74:6. The matching complete TE paragraphs are 52:5 and 74:7; the checked 52:6 and 74:6 do not contain the paired names. The native second label also appears to end in ז, unlike the accepted ו. The English uses the matched modern locations and preserves the old labels here, without claiming identical historical numbering. The exact 52:5 chain explicitly supplies Rabbi for Chama, his father Chanina, and Yissachar, supporting those titles in the quoted report. “If so” preserves Hyman’s inference about generation, not an independent chronological finding.

The remaining bibliography is carried as Hyman gives it and was not independently checked in this bounded review. The Shir HaShirim פ״ד is left unconverted: the earlier suggestion that it was another chapter 4 is withdrawn, while a verse/section interpretation is not silently adopted. The other short numerical labels and the stray conjunction in ובמדרש ותהלים do not license new modern references; the latter is rendered as the work title Midrash Tehillim.
